content.title: Sign in successfully as standard_user
content.intent: Prove a valid full-access credential establishes an authenticated session and reaches the appropriate standard banking experience.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp for the valid active-credential partition, auth for the authentication boundary, and state_flow for the unauthenticated-to-authenticated transition. Web form and auth-gated profiles applied. No covering array was needed because outcome-changing credential states were split into separate scenarios; strength=3 was risk-judged because auth applies, but the effective interaction reduced to a single representative credential partition in this path.

parameters.password_visibility: toggle reveal then hide before submit

content.title: Reject an invalid username or password
content.intent: Prove invalid credentials do not grant access and produce an understandable failure state instead of an authenticated session.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp for the invalid-credential partition, negative for the failed-auth outcome, and auth for the protected-session boundary. Web form and auth-gated profiles applied. No covering array was needed because this path isolates one invalid credential class whose outcome differs from the valid personas.

content.title: Block normal access for locked_user
content.intent: Prove the locked persona receives a clear locked-state outcome and is not treated as a normal active session.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp for the locked credential partition, auth for access restriction, and negative for the denied-login outcome. Web form and auth-gated profiles applied. No covering array was needed because locked_user is a distinct outcome-changing persona that must be separated from both valid and generic-invalid authentication.

content.title: Sign in as admin_user and reach the admin view
content.intent: Prove the administrative credential establishes an authenticated session that exposes the intended administrative view rather than the standard-user experience.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp for the administrative credential partition, auth for the role boundary, and state_flow for the authenticated transition into a role-specific experience. Web form and auth-gated profiles applied. No covering array was needed because admin_user is a separate outcome-changing role path.

content.title: Sign in as slow_user and observe the loading state resolve
content.intent: Prove the slow-loading persona shows an understandable in-progress state during authentication and eventually resolves to its intended post-login experience.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: eqp for the slow-loading persona partition, state_flow for the in-progress-to-authenticated transition, and negative/error-profile thinking for the exceptional loading behavior that must still resolve correctly. Web form and auth-gated profiles applied. No covering array was needed because slow_user changes the observable outcome and therefore stands as its own scenario.

content.title: Use the login page with keyboard-accessible controls
content.intent: Prove the username and password fields expose accessible names, the password visibility control has an understandable accessible name, and Remember me, Sign In, and Forgot password are keyboard operable.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: a11y for accessible naming and keyboard operability, plus web-form because the surface is a documented login form. No covering array was needed because this scenario targets one accessibility-focused interaction path rather than outcome-changing credential combinations.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] Applied the web-form profile because the PRD defines a browser login page with username, password, Remember me, Sign In, and Forgot password controls.
[applicability] Applied the auth-gated profile because the use-case centers on establishing or denying authenticated access and role/state-specific post-login experiences.
[applicability] Applied a11y technique coverage because the PRD explicitly promises accessible names for login fields and keyboard operability for checkboxes and actionable controls.

[applicability] Did not apply boundary value analysis because the PRD provides no numeric or length bounds for username or password inputs and does not define required-field outcomes for empty submission.
[applicability] Did not apply the REST / GraphQL API profile because the grounded evidence for this use-case is the web login surface, not an endpoint contract.
[applicability] Did not apply i18n as a scenario family because this use-case's cited promises do not define locale-dependent login text, formatting, or translated variants.
[value_score] Highest-value core happy path: proves the main authentication boundary works for an active full-access user and can also exercise the login controls on the way in.
[value_score] High-value negative path: proves failed credentials do not grant access and produce the required understandable failure state instead of an authenticated session.
[value_score] High-value security path: locked_user is explicitly documented as a restricted authentication outcome that must not receive normal access.
[value_score] High-value role path: admin_user must land in an administrative experience rather than a standard-user session, so it checks auth-plus-role boundary behavior.
[value_score] High-value exceptional path: slow_user is the only persona that explicitly adds in-progress loading behavior during sign-in, which changes the observable flow.
[value_score] Important accessibility path: it is the clearest way to exercise the login surface's documented accessible names and keyboard operability promises without overloading another scenario.

[value_score] Useful surface-inspection path, but most of its control-presence coverage can be exercised inside the kept standard_user and accessibility scenarios, so it was evicted under the ceiling.

[value_score] Documented persona path, but its key downstream transfer restriction belongs more strongly to transfer assurance than to the authentication boundary itself, so it was evicted under the ceiling.

[value_score] Documented persona path, but negative-balance correctness is primarily dashboard/account-state assurance after login rather than the sign-in boundary itself, so it was evicted under the ceiling.
[value_score] Documented persona path, but the wrong-loan-total condition is primarily loan-data assurance after authentication and is less central to the login boundary under this scenario budget.
